AssumptionNotAppliedView.description: A named item with the reason it was not applied / not relativized.

AssumptionsView.description: What `sv verify-auto` did with the design's `assume` statements.

consistency.description: `consistent`, `contradictory` (no trace satisfies every applied assumption: every HOLDS is vacuous) or `unknown`; omitted when nothing was applied.

mode.description: `precondition` (the default: guarantees are checked on the traces that satisfy the applied assumptions), `check` (assumptions are checked like assertions) or `ignore`.

unapplied.description: Assumptions not applied, with the reason. The guarantees were checked without them.

unguarded.description: Guarantees checked WITHOUT the assumptions (their formula could not be relativized).

BottomReasonView.description:
monono ask 26 — WHY a property is `⊥`, machine-readable.

The complement to `unknown_cells`: that field says HOW MUCH of the cube space stayed undecided, this one says WHY nothing decided it. A consumer previously had the quantity and not the cause, so the only available move on a `⊥` was to try budget knobs blind.

Carried as a FIELD rather than a note deliberately: a consumer that does not know about a field cannot silently filter it out, and a consumer that does not know about a note routinely does — which is exactly how the equivalent `bottom-reason` note (shipped in mununu#492) never reached the reader it was written for.

budget.description:
mununu#553 ask 1 — which engine budget fired, for `engine-did-not-complete` only: `iteration` · `node` · `bit-cap` · `arena-safety` · `fixpoint-latency` · `arena-exhausted` · `wall-clock` · `unrecognised`.

Previously all eight arrived as one `kind` and could only be told apart by regexing `detail` — while the table above told gates to branch on `kind`.

budget_knob.description: The env knob to raise for `budget`, when raising one is the right response (e.g. `MUNUNU_BDD_ITER_BUDGET`). Absent when no knob applies.

detail.description: Human-readable one-liner. For `engine-did-not-complete` this is the ENGINE'S OWN abstention message, which names the budget it hit and its numbers — e.g. *"abstained on the ITERATION budget (1048577 > 1048576) … raise MUNUNU_BDD_ITER_BUDGET"*.

determinism.description:
mununu#553 ask 2 — **would the same command on the same commit abstain again?**

| value | what a gate should do | |---|---| | `reproducible` | a property of the PROBLEM. Pin the `unknown` honestly, or raise the budget `budget` names | | `host-dependent` | a property of the AFTERNOON. Treat as a **configuration result**, not a verdict about the design — the same command may DECIDE on a quieter machine | | `unestablished` | not determined. Do not read as either |

This is the field that makes a `⊥` actionable without string-matching `detail`. Note that `budget-expired` (the 15-min per-property and 1-h whole-run harness clocks) is **on by default**, so `host-dependent` is reachable on an ordinary run with nothing configured.

engine.description:
Portfolio label of the engine that failed, for `engine-did-not-complete` only.

Describes a WHOLE-RUN failure over the design; it does **not** assert that this property caused it. The claim is that this property is `⊥` and the engine most likely to have decided it stopped for the stated reason.

kind.description:
Stable kebab-case tag for gates. **Branch on this, never on the outcome alone** — every value below previously produced an identical `unknown` with `unknown_cells: 0`.

| tag | what a gate should do | |---|---| | `budget-expired` | **WALL-CLOCK budget** — retry with more time | | `memory-ceiling-exceeded` | the process-RSS ceiling (`MUNUNU_MAX_PROCESS_MEMORY_BYTES`). **More TIME cannot help** — needs more memory, a smaller cone, or a lower tier. Host-dependent *without* a clock: RSS varies with allocator state and neighbours | | `engine-did-not-complete` | branch on **`budget`** — it names which engine budget fired, and `detail` carries the engine's own numbers | | `engine-contradiction` | 🔴 **SOUNDNESS ALARM.** Two engines returned OPPOSITE definite verdicts; one is unsound. **Retrying is actively wrong.** Escalate, do not re-run | | `report-self-contradiction` | 🔴 **SOUNDNESS ALARM (mununu#579).** Two properties of the SAME model came back with definite verdicts that cannot both be right — one engine disagreeing with itself across properties, where `engine-contradiction` compares engines on one property. **Both** are withheld, deliberately: a contradiction says one verdict is broken, not which. **Retrying is actively wrong**, and so is believing whichever looks more plausible. Escalate | | `engine-crashed` | the engine process died. Not an abstention; report it | | `unestablished-initial-state` | 🔴 **the withheld VIOLATED.** The property's cone touches `registers` register(s) with no established cycle-0 value. A free start set over-approximates reachability, which licenses a definite `HOLDS` but never a definite `VIOLATED` — so the violation is withheld. **Retrying cannot help.** Since mununu#578 recoverable reset values are established automatically, so a register still free here has none to recover: it holds through reset, or it is a `--cutpoint` / blackboxed output (free at every cycle by construction). Supply an `init` via a sidecar, or drop the cutpoint | | `violation-over-free-leaves` | 🔴 **the withheld VIOLATED, again (mununu#750).** The violation was found through an undriven net — an unconnected wire or the output of a module missing from the source set, free at every cycle — so its trace (kept in `counterexample`) is a MAY-trace: the real driver may never produce those values. `detail` names the nets. **Retrying cannot help**; vendor the missing module or provide the driver. A deliberate cut — a `--cutpoint` or a `(* blackbox *)` stub — is not counted (mununu#578) | | `unestablished-initial-cubes` | **nothing decided (mununu#579).** The property's predicates have `registers` register(s) with no `init` line (plus any free inputs), and the cube path's initial cube set — the product of those free dimensions — is past the 16 it enumerates. An init-less register is free at cycle 0 on every engine; supply an `init` via a sidecar (or let reset-gating establish it) and re-run. **Retrying cannot help.** | | `safety-shape-not-reducible` | the property's SHAPE is outside the rescue lane — a bigger budget **cannot** help. Reshape, or add a reducer | | `no-state-model-non-safety` | zero state registers; a modelling issue, not an engine cap | | `not-attempted` | filtered out before any engine ran | | `unclassified-bottom` | cause not established — do **not** treat as distinct-from-abstain |

A gate that retries every `unknown` with raised budgets spins forever on `safety-shape-not-reducible` and `no-state-model-non-safety`, and re-runs an unsoundness on `engine-contradiction`.

registers.description:
mununu#577 — how many registers in THIS property's cone have no established cycle-0 value, for `unestablished-initial-state` and `unestablished-initial-cubes` only.

Per-property, from the property's own cone — not a whole-design count — so it is the number that sizes the remedy. It is a field for the same reason `budget` is: the count is otherwise only inside `detail`'s prose, and a gate that greps prose for a number is the defect mununu#553 was filed against.

CellSource.description: Where a trace cell lives in the RTL (2026-10-29).

assigned.description: The `always` block(s) of the flop(s) driving a register; empty for an input.

cell.description: The cell as the trace names it (the net; a hierarchical name keeps its dots).

CexCellView.description: One register's concrete value in a counterexample state. mununu#723 — a cell wider than 64 bits was silently absent from the trace (OpenTitan edn's 109-bit `tl_i`, the bus write behind the fatal alert). `value` is unchanged for every cell that fits 64 bits — exactly the cells that were listed before — and `null` for a wider value; `hex` and `bits` are always present.

hex.description: `0x` + the value zero-padded to the cell's width — the form that always holds it.

value.description: The value when it fits 64 bits, else `null` (read `hex`).

ExpectationFailureView.description: mununu#537 — one unmet claim. `property` is absent for a run-level claim (the count).

ExpectationResultView.description:
mununu#537 — the verdict on a caller's declared expectations.

`satisfied: false` corresponds to CLI exit code **4** — "a verdict was not what you claimed", deliberately distinct from a failed run (1) and from the ordinary verdict gate (2 / 3).

FaultSiteView.description: One fault site of the posture (`diagnostics.fault_sites[]`).

register.description: The register, as the model names it.

rows.description: The security-countermeasure rows this site serves (`sec-cm` only).

selected_by.description: `"explicit"` (named on the request), `"instance-prefix"` (a `sec-cm` site inside the fault flag's own instance) or `"cone-fallback"` (every cell the flag compares).

width.description: Its width in bits (0 when the posture was not applied — a zero budget).

auto_provided_stubs.description: Cut flop-primitive modules for which a behavioral stub was auto-injected so the register survives the lift (e.g. `prim_sparse_fsm_flop`).

blackboxed_modules.description: Modules instantiated without a body, cut to free inputs (registers they drive are not modeled as state). Empty for a self-contained design.

config_values.description: mununu#536 — config inputs pinned for this run, each `"<signal>=<value>"`. A verdict under a pin is a claim about THAT configuration only, so the scope ships with it.

cutpoints.description: mununu#536 — signals cut to free inputs by `--cutpoint`: the control slice these verdicts were reached under.

fault_model.description: The fault-injection posture this run was under (`faults` / `fault_model`), as one label; `null` without one. A verdict under a posture is a claim about the design WITH an adversary at the listed sites, so the scope ships with it.

fault_sites.description: The registers the adversary may corrupt under the posture. Empty without one.

frontend.description: `"read_verilog + sv2v"`, `"yosys-slang (read_slang)"`). `--frontend auto` picks one silently and the two paths differ in SOUNDNESS on partial writes (#464/#465), so "which lift produced this verdict?" is a question the payload must answer. It was previously reachable only as `lift-frontend` note prose.
frontend.title: 466 / mununu#536 — the RTL front end that produced the lift (e.g.

frontend_fallback_reason.description: attempt's error. `None` when there was no fallback.
frontend_fallback_reason.title: 466 — when `--frontend auto` FELL BACK (an earlier front end errored), the prior

gated_resets.description: Reset inputs pinned inactive at the model level (`"<signal>=<value>"`), with their `disable iff` guards dropped from the formulas. Empty when reset-gating is off or no `disable iff` reset was recognized.

lift_retry.description: The lift rerun its yosys script with `opt_clean` before `write_btor` after the BTOR backend reported a topological loop (yosys-slang `$buf` cells; the model is the same design) — the reason, else `None`. The `lift-retry` note carries the same text.

merged_clock_domains.description: The clock domains `merge_clock_domains` lifted onto one clock, each `"<net> (<edge>, <n> cells)"`; empty for a single-clock design. Non-empty means every verdict assumes the domains tick together (the `clock-domains-merged` note).

source_map.description: Whether the rows' traces carry RTL source lines, and why not when they do not (2026-10-29).

state_register_count.description: Number of state register lines in the lifted model.

bottom_reason.description: monono ask 26 — why an `unknown` (⊥) property was not decided. `None` for a definite outcome. See [`BottomReasonView`].

decided_by.description:
Which portfolio engine produced this property's DEFINITE verdict. `None` for `⊥`.

**A verdict's PROVENANCE, per property.** The companion to `bottom_reason`: that says why a `⊥` happened, this says who answered when one did not.

**Why a gate should read it even when the verdict is `holds`.** Measured: at high arena occupancy a run still returned `holds`, but the exact engine dropped out and an abstracting engine supplied the verdict — sound under that engine's posture, but the **precision tier moved silently**. A gate pinning `holds` sees `holds` either way. Comparing this field against the previous run is how a consumer notices.

Previously available only as `decided-by:<engine>=<count>` in a report-level note: an AGGREGATE, which cannot say WHICH property changed tier, and filterable besides.

detail.description:
Human-readable detail: `"N cell(s)"` (violated/unknown) or the skip reason.

**Prefer the structured fields below.** This is prose and stays only so existing consumers keep working; a gate that needs the figure should read `false_cells` / `unknown_cells` / `skip_reason` rather than parsing this string.

false_cells.description: mununu#536 — the cell count behind a `violated` verdict, machine-readable. `None` for every other outcome.

formula.description: The property as its author wrote it when that was not mu-calculus — an `@mununu_guarantee ltl …` row shows its LTL (2026-10-29) — otherwise the mu-calculus the engine decided (every SVA row, plain annotation body and template). `formula_language` says which; `translated` carries the mu-calculus whenever `formula` is not it.

label.description:
mununu#544 — the assertion's SV label, when it has one.

This is what the author wrote (`a_reseed_only_at_a_span_edge:`), so it survives a reorder and a rename becomes a hard error instead of a silent re-point. Absent for an unlabelled assertion and for every `@mununu_guarantee` annotation (which carry no name today).

name.description: Positional name: `<module>_sva_<index>` (or `ann_guarantee_<index>`). An insertion mid-file re-points every later one — prefer `label` when pinning an expectation.

seeded_predicates.description: The cube predicates auto-seeded for this property (atom strings).

skip_reason.description: mununu#536 — why a `skipped` property was not evaluated. `None` for every other outcome.

trace.description: The counterexample ([`Trace`]) of a Violated property: for safety, the reset → violation path (empty `cycle`) native BMC re-derives whichever engine decided it (absent when none lies within the bound); D1.8b — a stall lasso for a bare `AF p` decided by the exact engine; A.4 — the unreachable target of a bare `EF p`.

translated.description: The mu-calculus the engine decided, present only when `formula` is written in another language (an `ltl` row). A tool that re-parses formulas reads this and falls back to `formula` when it is absent.

unknown_cells.description:
mununu#536 — the cell count behind an `unknown` (⊥) verdict, machine-readable. `None` for every other outcome.

This is the "cell/budget figure that accompanies a ⊥" the issue asks for: a ⊥ is a statement about how much of the cube space stayed undecided, and a consumer tracking whether refinement is helping needs the number, not a sentence containing it.

vacuity.description:
mununu#599 — a recoverability guarantee (`AG EF(P)`) that HOLDS, judged against the other verdicts in the same report. Present only on such a guarantee, and only when another property speaks to it; see [`VacuityView`].

**Read this next to `outcome == "holds"`.** `AG EF good: HOLDS` beside its non-vacuity witness `EF good': VIOLATED` is the vacuous pass a two-sided gate exists to prevent; it used to be visible only to a reader who checked witnesses by habit. The verdict does not change — a vacuous HOLDS is a true HOLDS on the model — the field says what it is worth.

ReplayResultView.description: The replay's verdict: the bench ran under Verilator and compared the trace cycle by cycle, or could not run and says why (2026-10-29).

assertions.description: Verilator's `Assertion failed` lines: the design's own assertion firing on the final state.

checks.description: The (cycle, register) comparisons the bench makes.

log.description: The bench's own lines: verdict, mismatches, assertions, the VCD line.

reason.description: Why the replay could not run (`unavailable`): Verilator or `make` missing, a compile error.

vcd_bytes.description: `replay.vcd`'s size in bytes, when `make trace` wrote it.

SourceLoc.description: A place in the RTL: the file's basename and a line (yosys's `src` keeps the path and the column; the report keeps what a reader opens).

SourceMapView.description: Whether rows and traces carry RTL source lines (2026-10-29): `available` when the netlist's lines are the RTL's (yosys-slang and yosys's `read_verilog` both stamp them), `unavailable` with the reason when they are not (sv2v preprocessed the source first).

makefile.description: `Makefile`; it names the sources as the request named them.

skipped.description: Cells left out of the comparison, with the reason.

Trace.description: The one counterexample shape of 0.5, shared by every verb that returns a path: RTL rows fill `state` / `inputs` / `faults`, CTXDSL rows fill `state_name` / `labels`. A two-player strategy stays its own object, and the counterstrategy graph stays a view.

loop_start.description: For a `lasso`: the index into `steps` the last step loops back to.

sources.description: Where each cell the trace shows lives in the RTL (2026-10-29): the legend, in the order of the first step's cells. Empty when the source map is unavailable (`diagnostics.source_map`).

unreachable_target.description: For `unreachable`: the target atoms no path reaches.

hex.description: The value in hexadecimal, at any width.

value.description: The value written, when it fits 64 bits.

oneOf.description: Reset → the failing step (a safety violation).
Reset → a prefix → a cycle repeated forever (`loop_start` marks it): a liveness stall.
Reset → a closed trap the target is never reached from again (a refuted `AG EF`).
No path: the `unreachable_target` atoms are never reached from reset (a refuted `EF`).
Reset → the injections of a fault attack that reaches its target (`steps[].faults`).

dir.description: Where the CLI wrote the files (`--emit-testbench DIR/<property>`); absent over HTTP.

gtkw.description: `replay.gtkw` — a GTKWave save file listing the clock, the trace's inputs and the registers it names, so `gtkwave replay.vcd replay.gtkw` opens on the scene (2026-10-29).

result.description: The bench built and run (`--replay` / `replay: true`); absent when not requested.

TraceStep.description: One step of a [`Trace`]: the state at `cycle` and what drives the step out of it.

inputs.description: The input assignment of this cycle (RTL), so the trace can be replayed.

labels.description: The labels of the transition out of this step (CTXDSL).

monitor.description: Cells the verifier added to the model (see [`is_monitor_cell`]): the property monitor's latches, `$past` shadows, fault-rewrite state. Kept for debugging, apart from `state`.

state.description: Register cells (RTL); empty for a CTXDSL step, which names its state in `state_name`.

UnsupportedAssertionView.description: An assertion outside the supported fragment (mirrors `UnsupportedAssertion`).

VacuityView.description: mununu#599 — how a recoverability guarantee that HOLDS stands against the rest of its report.

detail.description: One line of prose. **Do not string-match it**; read `kind` and `witness`.

kind.description:
Machine-stable tag:

| `kind` | meaning | |---|---| | `invariant-target` | **vacuous.** The target is invariant in this report — `EF(¬P)` VIOLATED or `AG(P)` HOLDS beside `AG EF(P)` HOLDS — so the design never leaves `P` and no recovery is ever exercised. Consistent; the HOLDS stands and says nothing about recovery. | | `witness-refuted` | **not shown non-vacuous.** A reachability over the guarantee's register at another value (`EF(st_q == S_WAIT)`) is VIOLATED in the same report. It does not make the guarantee false; if that property is the guarantee's non-vacuity witness, the pair is a failed gate, not a pass. | | `antecedent-unreachable` | **vacuous.** A security-countermeasure chain (`$rose(X) \|-> ##[0:k] alert`) HOLDS, and under the fault posture the reach portfolio proved `X` never rises on this model (the un-faulted lift's fault flags are synthesis constants). `witness` is the row itself. |

witness.description: The property (`name`) whose verdict establishes it.

detail.description: Longer explanation (the why + the soundness/scope implication).

property.description:
mununu#548 O-2 — the property this note is ABOUT, when it is about one.

Absent for a model-level note (reset-gating, control-slice, parameter overrides): those describe the lift, not a property.

**Group notes by this, not by parsing `summary`.** The name used to appear only as a `"<name>: "` prefix inside the prose, so a consumer joining on it inherited two bugs: a property whose name prefixes another's (`sva_1` vs `sva_10`) matched the wrong note, and any rewording of the note's opening silently broke the join.

assumptions.description: OpenTitan coverage, Phase 4 — what the run did with the design's SVA `assume` statements. Omitted when the design has none.

build.description: mununu#715 — the full commit sha of the binary that produced this report. Omitted when the build was not told its commit; never a guess. The `--version` line carries its short form.

build_clean.description: mununu#715 — `true` when no tracked file differed from `build` at build time. Present exactly when `build` is.

diagnostics.description: Model-level diagnostics: state-register count + black-boxed (cut) modules. Lets a SKIPPED outcome point at its root cause.

expectations.description:
mununu#537 — the result of checking this run against the caller's declared expectations. `None` (and omitted) when no expectations were declared, in which case the ordinary verdict gate applies.

Present so a consumer learns **which** claim failed without parsing prose.

notes.description: H.J — human-facing provenance notes: every abstraction / scoping decision the run made (config concretizations, reset-gating, flop stubs, cut modules, the abstraction posture, the coverage summary), so a verdict's scope and caveats are explicit in the payload.

unsupported.description: Assertions that did not translate (reuses the extract-sva view shape; `kind` is `None` here).
